correctness.rationale: For d>=2, 0<q<1 and 0<=L<1+q, the nested case is trivial. In the pole case the small-ball squared-distance surplus is exactly -delta(s+1/d)^2 and the large-ball boundary maximum is attained only at s=1 under an explicit sharp inequality; L(h) is strictly increasing. In the two-latitude case both ball surpluses are exactly negative squares, and L(t) is strictly decreasing because the differentiated rational expression has explicitly positive numerator factor T. Exact normalized contact weights have mean 0 and second moment I_d/d, proving global maximum volume and uniqueness by John’s criterion, regardless of competitor orientation. The real packaged program passed 675 boundary-distance and covariance diagnostics. Finite checks are corroborative only.

value.rationale: An unequal-ball lens is a basic natural full-dimensional convex object. The theorem gives its unique maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid, including all boundary contacts, with exact scalar monotone reconstruction for every dimension. Its sharp q=1/d radius screening is a structural dichotomy not implied by the general existence/SDP characterization; for small radius ratios the larger ball contributes only an axial pole arbitrarily near tangency, whereas above the threshold a second latitude emerges at a precise separation. The contact product -1/d is a meaningful dimension-wide invariant, rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
